Methods

The following text can be adapted for publications.

Methods Boilerplate

The following text can be used as a starting point for the methods section of a publication. Please verify and adapt as needed.

Temporal interference stimulation simulations were performed with TI-Toolbox for subject ernie using montage docs_example. The report describes temporal interference (TI); the modeled electrode pairs were E034-E020 and E095-E070 at 1.0 mA per pair [Grossman2017].

Electrodes were modeled as ellipse 8x8 mm electrodes with 4 mm conductive gel and 2 mm rubber layers. Electrode positions were derived from the EEG net GSN-HydroCel-185.csv. Subject-specific head models and finite-element electric-field solves used the SimNIBS/CHARM workflow with scalar conductivity and default SimNIBS tissue conductivities [Saturnino2019; Puonti2020; Saturnino2015; Jurcak2007].

TI-Toolbox post-processing generated TI_max and TI_normal field outputs and exported mesh or NIfTI derivatives when available. Report metadata were reloaded from saved simulation provenance. Software versions and audit metadata are listed in the report, following BIDS-style derivative provenance [BIDS2016].

  3. [Saturnino2019] Saturnino GB, Puonti O, Nielsen JD, Antonenko D, Madsen KH, Thielscher A. SimNIBS 2.1: a comprehensive pipeline for individualized electric field modelling for transcranial brain stimulation. Journal of Neural Engineering. 2019;16(6):066006. [DOI]
  4. [Puonti2020] Puonti O, Van Leemput K, Saturnino GB, Siebner HR, Madsen KH, Thielscher A. Accurate and robust whole-head segmentation from magnetic resonance images for individualized head modeling. NeuroImage. 2020;219:117044. [DOI]
  5. [Saturnino2015] Saturnino GB, Antunes A, Thielscher A. On the importance of electrode parameters for shaping electric field patterns generated by tDCS. NeuroImage. 2015;120:25-35. [DOI]
  6. [Gaugain2023] Gaugain G, et al. Quasi-static approximation error of electric field analysis for transcranial current stimulation. Journal of Neural Engineering. 2023;20(1):016027. [DOI]
  7. [Jurcak2007] Jurcak V, Tsuzuki D, Dan I. 10/20, 10/10, and 10/5 systems revisited: their validity as relative head-surface-based positioning systems. NeuroImage. 2007;34(4):1600-1611. [DOI]
